title: "005 — Shape-driven tool result rendering"
---

## 005 — Shape-driven tool result rendering {#sec-005}

> **Status:** standing

**Goal.** Make expanded tool-result bodies readable by classifying each result through
one pure classifier returning exactly one shape — records, JSON, markdown, text, or short
prose — and rendering accordingly: URL-bearing records become a capped list of link cards
with the separate sources list folded in; markdown renders as markdown; other JSON
pretty-prints; anything unrecognized degrades to today's bounded raw view. Classification
precedence is fixed, tolerant of multi-part payloads joined without separators. Strictly
presentation-only: stored payloads are read-only inputs, so legacy chats render nicely
with zero data change.

**Why.** MCP mount code joins content parts with no separator, so concatenated JSON is
the normal case, and nothing between storage and screen parsed it. The same payload was
parsed again for the sources link list — links shown twice, once as a wall. Meanwhile the
constitution forbids UI-side per-tool special cases, ruling out hand-maintained branches
by tool name or server. Identity-blind shape detection was the only road that scales.

**Outcome & reversals.** Standing today: the classifier is named the single shape
authority in the current architecture docs — never tool identity, never a UI-side tool
list — with degradation structural: the raw view is the ladder's bottom rung, not an error
boundary around rendering. It replaced feature [#004](004-internal-area-unification.qmd#sec-004)'s result-body expander
section and swapped the floating toggle for the header row itself; for record shapes the
sources row is suppressed so exactly one list renders — partially retiring the separate
Sources list that [#001](001-brave-search-mcp.qmd#sec-001) had introduced (it survives for other shapes). Feature
[#006](006-ai-elements-adoption.qmd#sec-006) retained the body renderer untouched inside its new collapsible shell and
deliberately skipped a donor code-highlighting block to avoid a second path — a direct
endorsement. Nothing later overturns it.

**Learnings.**

- Classify payload shape, never tool identity: shape-based rendering survives every new
  tool without registry coupling.
- Build graceful degradation structurally — make the old-correct view the ladder's bottom
  rung instead of wrapping rendering in error handling.
- Share parsers between consumers so two views can never disagree about the payload.
- Read actual storage shape before designing APIs: a spec'd nested-field read would have
  silently seen nothing for every real row.
